Sublattice domination proves a finite threshold. The cited density bound and written right continuity give a positive critical density; positive isolation probability makes the lower threshold bound strict.

An embedded plane, the heavy-edge theorem, closed cuts and the cited inverse-square inputs give the classification. Sharpness identifies the susceptibility endpoint; finite-cluster atoms give continuity.
